page: Microsoft Azure E96as_v4 is an EASv4-family virtual machine powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, configured with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs via multithreading. The system is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 1376 GB drive, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the E96as_v4 demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core testing and PassMark CPU encryption. Memory performance is also notable, with PassMark memory scores ranking in the top 10% and small-block read-only memory bandwidth placing in the top 25%. However, large-block read and write memory bandwidths fall into the average range. Single-core performance is moderate, with Geekbench single-core and static web serving throughput registering in the middle 50%. Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core compiling, consistently rank in the top 25%.

From a resource density perspective, the E96as_v4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy workloads that do not require dedicated GPU acceleration. The primary tradeoff lies in its single-core performance and large-block memory bandwidth, which do not match its top-tier multi-core capabilities. This hardware profile is suited for database operations, memory-intensive enterprise applications, multi-threaded data processing, and moderate-scale language model inference.
